method: Thinker proposes missing capabilities; Challenger checks duplication, necessity, scope, and whether the need belongs in shared infrastructure or a downstream module.

findings.signal: Run 006 already exposed multiple email identities and future systems will need account, vendor, payment-source, device, cloud, and connector identities.
findings.riskIfMissing: Coverage claims become unreliable and the same account/source is represented differently across teams.
findings.challenger: Do not build a full identity platform; start with sourceId, owner, sourceType, account hint, connection state, authority scope, last verified, and coverage state.

findings.signal: Subscription, inbox, bills, documents, security, warranties, and follow-up all consume evidence from heterogeneous systems.
findings.riskIfMissing: Every team invents its own evidence format; reconciliation and audit become brittle.
findings.challenger: Extend the Run 006 evidence model rather than inventing a new event bus.

findings.signal: Multiple systems can detect issues but owner approvals currently live inside individual projects or chats.
findings.riskIfMissing: Important decisions become scattered; alerts tell the owner something is wrong without a single place to resolve it.
findings.challenger: This should not duplicate the Master Work Calendar; it stores decision state and approval authority, while calendar stores time commitments.

findings.signal: ChatGPT, SMS, email, and calendar escalation are already appearing in Run 006 and will recur everywhere.
findings.riskIfMissing: Duplicate alerts, inconsistent severity, channel sprawl, notification fatigue, and uncontrolled messaging cost.
findings.challenger: Extract only after Run 006 G6 validates the policy pattern; reuse severity, dedupe, cooldown, channel routing, and cost caps.

findings.signal: Projects repeatedly contain deferred actions, pending replies, prerequisites, approvals, and later-to-do items.
findings.riskIfMissing: Silent stalls and cognitive load persist even with good project records.
findings.challenger: Keep it small: waitingFor, owner, expectedBy, lastTouch, escalation rule, resolvedAt. Do not make another general task manager.

findings.signal: Work increasingly depends on infrastructure, credentials, gates, subscriptions, external accounts, and prior Factory runs.
findings.riskIfMissing: The system can prioritize tasks but cannot explain what unlocks the most downstream work.
findings.challenger: Represent dependencies as lightweight relations between projects/capabilities/actions; avoid a complex project-management engine.

findings.signal: A system may appear configured while credentials expire, workflows stop running, registers stop updating, or evidence goes stale.
findings.riskIfMissing: False confidence: the owner assumes coverage exists when the watcher itself is broken.
findings.challenger: Monitor last-success time, expected cadence, connector health, queue backlog, failure count, and coverage freshness; do not duplicate provider observability tools.

findings.signal: Agent systems consume SaaS subscriptions, API calls, hosting, SMS, credits, and infrastructure capacity across projects.
findings.riskIfMissing: Automation can be locally cheap but globally expensive; ROI and cost caps are hard to enforce.
findings.challenger: Do not build accounting software. Track expected cost, actual/estimated variable cost, owner-approved caps, and project attribution.

findings.signal: More systems will inspect email, financial evidence, documents, account metadata, and potentially personal administration records.
findings.riskIfMissing: The system may retain unnecessary sensitive material merely because ingestion is technically possible.
findings.challenger: Adopt minimal durable fields, retention classes, redaction rules, and source-specific prohibitions; reuse Run 006 raw-body minimization.

findings.signal: As workflows become persistent and multi-step, retries and partial failures will become normal operational events.
findings.riskIfMissing: Duplicate external actions, lost state, inconsistent registers, and manual cleanup after outages.
findings.challenger: Generalize SAFE execution contracts: idempotency keys, outbox, retry cap, replay boundary, recovery log.

findings.signal: Email contains obligations that are broader than subscriptions: deadlines, replies, invoices, approvals, appointments, documents, and account warnings.
findings.riskIfMissing: Run 006 solves only one class of inbox-derived obligation while the larger cognitive burden remains.
findings.challenger: Reuse the source registry and evidence envelope; do not create another inbox connector architecture.

findings.signal: It is easy to build more agents than are economically or cognitively useful.
findings.riskIfMissing: Automation accumulation: systems remain alive despite low value, unnecessary cost, or duplicated function.
findings.challenger: Measure exceptions caught, owner minutes saved, prevented loss, cost, false alerts, and usage; retire low-value capabilities.

challengedOutOrDeferred.idea: Separate manager for every administrative category immediately
challengedOutOrDeferred.reason: Would duplicate ingestion, evidence, alerts, approvals, and auditing. Build shared core first.
Combines discovery and authority in one boundary, increases blast radius, and conflicts with SAFE/governed execution.

challengedOutOrDeferred.idea: Replace Notion, Calendar, n8n, and project systems with a new all-in-one platform
challengedOutOrDeferred.reason: Current systems already provide useful canonical surfaces; integration and control-plane consistency have higher ROI than platform replacement.
